title: Enquirer’s Guide: What is an aperture?
summary: An aperture is an opening produced when optical alignment, surface preparation, and the right relation to a Referent meet exacting conditions.
author: The Enquirer’s Guide Desk
paragraphs: This entry from The Enquirer’s Guide answers a question often put to the Society: “What is an aperture?”
An aperture is an opening produced when optical alignment, surface preparation, and the right relation to a Referent meet exacting conditions.
Most are tiny or short lived. A bright point in a shadow is not sufficient proof that one has opened.

Readers should treat the answer as an introduction rather than a final authority. Eidetic science in Alderwick is reported through measurements, disputed interpretations and careful revisions, and a respectable enquiry may properly end with further questions.
